_doc: The standard switching plan (ACCOUNTS_PLAN_BUILD_STANDARD_SWITCHING), read by switching_plan.py and slot_allocator.py. Rules are data; each carries its provenance: [O] owner's words, [C] his question-card pick, [D] delegated (ours, under design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md), [A] agent proposal he has not ruled. [CA] the Conductor window's act under RIMMANDRAKE_ENACT_CONDUCTOR_MAY_DO_ALL_BUT_FIVE_ACTS (owner 2026-11-19): a change to the order or a leave line names what is lost if wrong and its undo (`lost: ...; undo: ...`), checked by selftest_switching_plan.py. Account names are the switcher's non-secret registry labels (~/.claude-accounts/accounts.tsv); reset times are NEVER written here: they are read from account_usage.py every pass.
_owner: [O] 2026-10-28 10:15 PDT: 'Use up both lukas.mandrake and mandrake.system of course down to ~2% for safety. Make sure not to overshoot and get stuck even if there is a surprise long-running subagent. then go idle until 1pm when you switch over to system.mandrake. Once steven.lewis resets, switch over to it and use it until 50%. Then use up system.mandrake to 2%, then lukas.mandrake to 2%. That's our first "standard switching plan."'
_order: [O] 2026-10-28 10:15 (see _owner): 'Once steven.lewis resets, switch over to it and use it until 50%. Then use up system.mandrake to 2%, then lukas.mandrake to 2%.' A fixed priority: the engine burns the FIRST account in this list that is eligible (measured, fresh, inside its window, above its line). steven is eligible only inside his window after his reset, down to leave_pct_left. When system resets, the machine goes to system even if lukas still has budget; a lower account's budget that expires first is given up (the owner 2026-10-28, on being left on lukas at 13:00: 'awkward').

steven._leave_pct_left: [C] 2026-10-28 10:20 card, Steven: 'Leave at 52% left' (his 10:15 words: 'use it until 50%'; the 2 points are the overshoot margin).
steven._window_h_after_reset: [O] 2026-10-27 'Dispatcher can use Steve up to 50% after a fresh reset only'; the 48 h reading of 'fresh' is [A] (slot_rules.json lent_accounts.steven.prefer_start_of_week_h). Outside this window the engine never switches to steven and switches off him if live.

floors._doc: [O] 2026-11-20 about 5:30 AM PST: "And yes for live runs finish past, absolutely. Actually 0.1% is even ok kept. We just don't want to crash to zero and get stuck. Please make that true everywhere." About 6 AM PST: "Agreed for 1% at the moment". So no account is driven to 0%: switch_away_pct_left is 1 (it was 0, his 2026-10-28 15:33 card 'Drain to 0%'), the lowest line the meter can see (8,749 stored readings, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-20, are all whole percents; design/specs/2026-11-20-account-drain/boundary.md). Live runs FINISH: a switch or a stop that falls due waits while a detached run is live; how an account ends is account_end (2026-11-24, which replaced hard_pct_left and drain_pct). lost: 1% of the system and lukas weeks is left unspent. undo: switch_away_pct_left 0. [D] wait_pct_left 2: the account we idle on until a reset keeps 2%, so the owner can still talk to a seat (card 10:20, Floor: '[No preference]'). blind_zero_pct [R] coordinator 2026-10-28 11:2x: once an account's last MEASURED reading is at or under 1%, a blind reading (failed /usage, usage-limit error, ESTIMATE, stale) counts as 0% and triggers the switch: never sit waiting on a meter that cannot read an exhausted account.

account_end._owner: [O] 2026-11-24 11:05 to 11:15 AM PST: 'At 2% no new work is started and "wrap it up cleanly and safely save your work" is sent to everyone. At 1% "emergency: record your state immediately and prepare for termination." Give it a beat... don't just kill at 1%. After a brief pause that has <10% chance of reaching 0% account, initiate the switch. Don't bother manually killing everything, it will happen all by itself, and you don't want to be yourself trapped in housekeeping.' Then: 'I agree with your switch when the last live run has ended when <2% remains. Correct, any account that has preserved space well above zero (usually only Steven's) does not need the emergency kill at all. Correct, wait for a reset if it's the last account.'
account_end._card: [C] 2026-11-24, How long should the pause at 1% be? -> Sized from the burn rate, with his words: 'that may also initiate the "no new work / save now" warning up at 3% as well if the burn is going crazy fast. Scale both 3/2% (initiate saves) warning and the time-constant post 1% based on load. If the reading is believed to be stale, default to safe values. TELL THE PROCESSES these numbers. Estimate how long they have to complete their saves. It may influence their choices.'
account_end._numbers: warn_pct, warn_fast_pct, emergency_pct, pause_share (a fifth), pause_from_pct and pause_max_s (3 min) are [O]/[C] above; the rest is [D]. Each number's danger and evidence: design/specs/2026-11-24-account-end/boundary.md LIMITS. lost: a floor account may end a little above 1%, at most 2 points a week; undo: revert the commits of RIMMANDRAKE_BUILD_ACCOUNT_END_WARN_SAVE_PAUSE_SWITCH_SIZED_BY_BURN.

_pull_drain_max_s: [O] 2026-11-20 about 5:30 AM PST: "And yes for live runs finish past, absolutely. Actually 0.1% is even ok kept. We just don't want to crash to zero and get stuck. Please make that true everywhere." A switch made ABOVE the line (a priority or reset pull, nothing spent) waits while a detached run is live, so the run finishes on its own account and keeps its prompt cache (the switch stops every Claude process; 2026-11-18: 9 resumes after a stop and a switch missed the cache, 4.73M weighted on their first turns). It waits at most this many seconds after the first drain notice. Danger of the bound: a run that never ends keeps every new start waiting and the machine off the account the order wants (steven's window is 48 h). Evidence: 724 detached runs, measured 2026-11-20, ran p50 24 min, p95 122, max 804; 7200 s lets 95 of 100 finish. With no live run the pull switch goes at once. Replaces checkpoint_grace_s (240 s, then SIGTERM). lost: a pull switch can come up to 2 h late; undo: pull_drain_max_s 0 (the switch goes at once, killing live runs).
_soft_margin_pct: [C] card 10:20, Overshoot: 'Soft line, then hard stop'. At line + 2%: a notice, publish and finish; a new detached run still starts (no new start comes at the warning line, account_end). lost: nothing is refused at the notice; undo: none needed.
_switch_lead_min: [A] a switch that a reset will cause (system at its reset, steven at his) raises the same soft notice this many minutes before the reset, so work is published before the windows close.

fresh._doc: [A] (brief 2026-10-28): within near_pct of a line, the engine polls the meter itself rather than trust a reading older than max_age_min.

_window_margin_min: [R] GPT review round 9: a windowed account (steven) is no switch target in the last 10 min of its window, so a slow arm + use never lands after the window closed (live there, it is switched away early).
_pool_pacing: [C] card 10:20, Pacing: 'Pace the whole pool BECAUSE it spreads out the human review time cleanly to inform the process in a timely manner.' slot_allocator paces on what this plan will still spend (steven down to its leave line inside its window, the others to their floors) over the hours to each deadline.

exceptions._why: lukas keeps the standard floors (warning at 2, switch at 1 or when the last run ends) on the owner's word of 2026-11-24 about 4:50 PM PST: 'Don't switch it until 1% ok? I want to use up as much as possible, as always.'; a line of 8 set at 4:40 PM on his 'no more work on lukas' was removed 10 minutes later. Order changed to system, lukas, steven on the owner's word of 2026-11-24 2:13 PM PST: 'No... use up Lukas first. We're already here, and nothing needs to be restarted. Just do it right!' (lukas was live at 18% left; the old order made the engine drain lukas for a preference switch to steven and refuse every new run for 49 minutes); undo: set the order back to system, steven, lukas. [CA] steven's leave line raised 3 to 5 on the owner's word of 2026-11-21 5:4x PM PST, with steven at 5% left and a switch pending: 'Go ahead and wind down that switch and get it done. I'm about to lose access and would like to see it work.'; lost: about 2 points of steven's week go unused; undo: set it back to 3. Before that: carries the owner's order of 2026-11-20 about 4:15 PM PST: 'Steven has just authorized us to use his account FULLY as the next act. He has a full account reset available and intends to use it before it expires, so we do NOT switch to lukas.mandrake next, we switch back to Steven and burn it as fully as we safely can.' and 'Do not switch right now! Use up this account first ok?'; leave lines at 3 on the owner's word of 2026-11-20 4:27 PM PST: 'Of course you should raise it to 3% to give them room to finish towards 1%. Otherwise you're ensuring lost work.'; lost: steven's week is spent to about 1% instead of 52%; undo: delete this exception

_exceptions: [D] dated, self-expiring exceptions to the rules above (switching_plan.at(): the plan in force at a time). Each needs an id, `from` and `until` as ISO times with their UTC offset (at most 7 days apart), a `_why` with its provenance, and changes `order` (a reordering of the standing accounts) and/or `accounts.<name>.leave_pct_left` / `window_h_after_reset`; optional `ends_at_reset_of` ends it at that account's first reset after `from`, read from the meter. The guard (exception_problems) refuses a broken one, and overlapping ones, which are then never applied: the standing plan stands and every decision names the refusal (exception_refused). slot_allocator.lent_allowance reads the same exception for a lent account. An expired exception is inert and may be deleted.
